### Discovery findings

- Evidence and preliminary recommendations recorded in `docs/admin-workspace-discovery.md`. Shared all-admin reads already exist; creator/initiator identity fields do not. Issue-keyed generation and cost-event upserts are not a per-attempt history. Full-run failures have best-effort generic reporting, while early/prerequisite failures, cancellations, missed reporting and focused runs need independent coverage/reconciliation. Lists are capped at 100 invitations/200 generation records without cursor pagination.
- Preliminary direction: persistent invite-only application admin membership with Neon Auth evaluated against the actual Worker/session boundary; preserve existing coordinator/engine/data while introducing explicit client/attempt/actor entities. No blind database replacement or Access-policy weakening. Missing historical actors must remain unknown unless recovered from verified evidence.
- Validation: source inspection only, including current schemas/handlers, tracker helper, full/focused workflows, existing tests, historical dashboard progress and current Neon documentation. No test/build/browser run, live client data access, provider request, schema provisioning, product-code edit, merge or deployment. Task remains open pending design approval.

### 19:20 UTC - Tracking Task 1 ready for controller review, not shipment

- Implemented pure shared wire types in `src/lib/admin-contracts.ts`; additive SQLite attempts/dispatches/events/health, immutable bindings, canonical executed identity, source-version outcome projection, attempt-local cost aggregates and cursor queries in `worker/src/generation-attempts.ts`. `worker/src/generation-ledger.ts` only initializes/delegates the new model; existing tables, methods and hero behavior are unchanged. Added 19 real Worker tests in `worker/test/admin-attempts.test.ts`.
- TDD evidence: initial new-suite RED was 12/12 failures for missing RPCs. Additional self-review RED runs caught delivery-none suppressing evidence, cross-key stale source updates, invented execution timestamps, partial-binding collisions returning SQLite internals, and ignored late failure details. All were fixed and reverified. Eviction/re-entry, dispatch initial-attempt retention, event-batch rollback, 251-attempt and 451-event cursor traversal are covered.
- Ruling: `observedAt` is an evidence version, not proof of execution start/completion; events do not invent those times. Explicit matching-result snapshots can fill missing completion time and newer failure details while keeping the authoritative execution lock. Cost if wrong: the Task 3 adapter must supply actual run timestamps rather than deriving them from observation arrival.
- Ruling: null association fields mean no new evidence, not clearing a binding. A new alias for an already-bound execution returns the canonical ID; colliding two existing records returns conflict rather than silently merging historical queue evidence. Unknown actors may bind once; known actor snapshots cannot be rewritten. Repository identity is case-insensitive. Search currently covers available attempt/client/request/run/repository/issue references, not business fields owned by Task 2.
- Test harness finding: negative RPC calls were correctly rejected but this installed Cloudflare Vitest wrapper also emitted unhandled rejections. Negative assertions now run inside the real DO with `runInDurableObject`, while positive reads/writes exercise RPC; no error suppression or production workaround added. A small test-only environment compatibility cast is centralized in the helper. Dataset seeding uses the real DO method inside its context to avoid hundreds of test-RPC round trips under CPU contention.
- Final local verification: `npx vitest run --config vitest.worker.config.ts worker/test/admin-attempts.test.ts worker/test/generation-ledger.test.ts` passed 2 files/24 tests (19 new + 5 existing); `npm run test:worker -- --maxWorkers=1` passed all 18 files/195 tests; `npm run check:worker` passed both TypeScript projects; `git diff --check` passed. Node v24.20.0 PATH used for every Node command.
